blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: A ConfigMap stores settings as keys and values. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: Keeping settings outside the image means you can change them without rebuilding the app.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: Pods find the ConfigMap by this name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: The name Pods use to find these settings
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings

blocks.title: The settings
blocks.what: Each line under data is one setting: a key and a text value.
blocks.why: Settings stay readable and easy to change. ConfigMaps are for normal settings, not passwords.
blocks.ifRemoved: The ConfigMap is created empty, so the app gets no settings.
blocks.comment: The settings: one key and value per line
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue

blocks.title: A Pod to read them
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a Pod called settings-demo.
blocks.why: The Pod shows how an app reads the settings.
blocks.ifRemoved: The file only stores settings. Nothing uses them yet.
blocks.comment: A Pod that reads the settings
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: settings-demo

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: A small busybox container prints the greeting, then waits.
blocks.why: The greeting stays empty until the next block passes in the settings.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.comment: A container that prints the greeting
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: settings-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $GREETING && sleep 3600"]

blocks.title: Settings as variables
blocks.what: envFrom turns every key in the ConfigMap into an environment variable in the container.
blocks.why: Apps commonly read settings from environment variables, so no code change is needed.
blocks.ifRemoved: The container starts without the settings, and the greeting is empty.
blocks.comment: Turn every setting into an environment variable
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: settings-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $GREETING && sleep 3600"]
      envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: app-settings

blocks.title: Settings as files: the volume
blocks.what: A volume makes the ConfigMap available to the Pod as files, one file per key.
blocks.why: Some apps read settings from files instead of variables.
blocks.ifRemoved: Nothing changes in the container yet. The next block mounts the files.
blocks.comment: Make the settings available as files
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: settings-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $GREETING && sleep 3600"]
      envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: app-settings
  volumes:
    - name: settings
      configMap:
        name: app-settings

blocks.title: Settings as files: the mount
blocks.what: The mount puts the files in the folder /etc/settings inside the container.
blocks.why: Mounted files update when the ConfigMap changes. Environment variables only change when the Pod restarts.
blocks.ifRemoved: The volume exists, but the container cannot see the files.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: app-settings
data:
  GREETING: "Hello from a ConfigMap"
  COLOR: blue
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: settings-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.37.0
      command: ["sh", "-c", "echo $GREETING && sleep 3600"]
      envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: app-settings
      volumeMounts:
        - name: settings
          mountPath: /etc/settings
  volumes:
    - name: settings
      configMap:
        name: app-settings

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API version for this object. ConfigMaps and Pods are both in the core v1 API.
notes.ConfigMap:kind: The type of object to create. A ConfigMap stores settings as text.
notes.Pod:kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.ConfigMap:metadata.name: The ConfigMap's name. Pods refer to it by this name.
notes.Pod:metadata.name: The Pod's name. It must be unique among Pods in the same namespace.
notes.data: The settings. Each key becomes a variable name or a file name.
notes.data.GREETING: A setting with spaces in its value, so the value is in quotes.
notes.data.COLOR: A one-word setting. Quotes are optional for simple text.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container's name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.containers[].command: The command to run. It prints the greeting, then sleeps so you can look around.
notes.spec.containers[].envFrom: Load environment variables from another object.
notes.spec.containers[].envFrom[].configMapRef: Use every key in a ConfigMap as an environment variable.
notes.spec.containers[].volumeMounts: Where volumes appear inside this container.
notes.spec.containers[].volumeMounts[].name: The volume to mount. It matches a name under volumes.
notes.spec.containers[].volumeMounts[].mountPa: The folder inside the container where the files appear.
notes.spec.volumes: Storage the Pod's containers can mount.
notes.spec.volumes[].name: The volume's name. Mounts refer to this name.
notes.spec.volumes[].configMap: Fill this volume from a ConfigMap, one file per key.
notes.spec.volumes[].configMap.name: The ConfigMap to read: app-settings.

tryIt.result: Prints configmap/app-settings created and pod/settings-demo created.
Prints blue, read from the mounted file.
Removes the ConfigMap and the Pod.

sources.title: Configure a Pod to use a ConfigMap
